title: Handover Synthesis and Cascade Communication Playbook
author: Arjun Mehta
body:
Overview:
This playbook defines a compact, repeatable handover-and-synthesis process plus a layered (cascade) customer/status communication pattern for incidents that affect Redwood Inference service availability, latency, or quality. It is intended for on-call responders, bridge operators, and service stewards.

Purpose:
- Reduce cognitive load during long incidents by standardizing what must be captured during each shift and handover.
- Provide clear escalation thresholds and deliverables for external communications and status page updates.
- Ensure post-incident artifacts (evidence, timelines, mitigations) are created reliably to accelerate root cause analysis and corrective actions.

Scope:
Applies to all production-facing incidents for Redwood-hosted inference endpoints, Dedicated pools, and Private control plane components. Not intended for purely local developer environment issues.

Roles & Responsibilities:
- First Responder: owns initial triage and short-term mitigation (15–60 minutes).
- Bridge Operator: responsible for running the coordination bridge, authoring status updates, and ensuring handover notes are complete.
- Service Steward: senior on-call who oversees escalation to engineering leads and customer success.
- SRE/Runtime Pager: executes cross-region mitigations and runbook actions.
- Customer Success Liaison: prepares customer-facing language for high-impact incidents.

Incident lifecycle (compact):
1) Detection & Triage
   - Verify alert signal (metrics, SLO alarms, user reports).
   - Classify impact: Latency SLO, Availability SLO, Model-quality regression, or Data plane error.
   - Assign severity (P0–P3) per the standard severity matrix.

2) Contain & Stabilize
   - Apply pre-approved mitigations from runbook (traffic-shed, fallthrough to model-variant, scale-up reserved pool).
   - If mitigation not available, open a mitigation action with owner and ETA.

3) Communicate (internal & external) — follow cascade template below.

4) Restore & Verify
   - Gradual recovery with canary checks; confirm SLO telemetry returns to normal for 30 minutes.

5) Handover & Synthesis (end of shift / major milestone)
   - Use the Handover Checklist below.

6) Post-incident: create postmortem draft within 48 hours (synthesis + timeline + actions).

Handover & Synthesis Checklist (to be completed on every shift handoff):
- Incident ID and current severity.
- One-line summary of current system state (e.g., "partial region degradation: us-west-2 inference latency 95p 2.6s").
- Active mitigations in place and owner for each.
- Remaining unknowns / hypothesis list (max 5).
- Key evidence collected and links (metrics dashboards, flamegraphs, kernel traces).
- Customer impact summary (tenants affected, percentage of traffic).
- Required next steps and estimated time to next milestone.
- Bridge log excerpt and pointer to artifacts.
- Risks and recommended escalation (e.g., open exec alert if >2 hours without improvement).

Handover template (copy into incident ticket or bridge chat):
- Handover from: <name> (time, timezone)
- Handover to: <name>
- Incident ID: <INC-YYYYMMDD-n>
- Severity: <P0|P1|P2|P3>
- State summary: <one sentence>
- Active mitigations: <bulleted list with owners>
- Evidence pointers: <links>
- Hypotheses: <ranked list>
- Next milestones: <time + objective>
- Customer comm status: <last update time>

Cascade communication pattern (when to update whom):
- Internal short pulse (T+10m): initial triage note to the incident channel.
- Customer notice (T+30m) if >1% traffic or latency SLO breach continues and customer-visible errors exist.
- Status page: publish at T+30m for major incidents; hourly updates thereafter until resolved.
- Executive alert: send when incident is P0 or unresolved after 1 hour.

Status page update rules (minimum fields):
- Title: short, customer-facing (what and where)
- Impact: severity and scope (tenants/regions)
- Mitigation: what we are doing now
- ETA: next update time and expected recovery window
- Links: postmortem placeholder, incident ticket, community forums if applicable

Sample status page initial message (copy to status tool):
Title: Partial regional degradation affecting inference latency (us-west-2)
Impact: Requests routed to us-west-2 may see elevated latency (95p ~2.5s). Some customer requests may be delayed but not dropped.
Mitigation: Traffic is being routed to a prioritized pool and we are autoscaling dedicated capacity.
ETA: We will provide an update at 15:00 UTC.
Links: https://redwood/internal/inc/INC-20251116-4

Customer communication templates (for Customer Success / CSR use)
1) Initial customer notice (concise):
Subject: Brief service impact affecting inference in us-west-2
Body: "We are currently investigating elevated inference latency affecting some requests in the us-west-2 region. Our engineering team is actively mitigating and routing traffic to reduce impact. We will provide an update within 30 minutes. If you are seeing specific errors, please reply with any request IDs or timestamps. — Redwood Operations"

2) Escalation / targeted customer message:
Subject: Update on service impact — mitigation in progress
Body: "Update: We have routed affected traffic to a prioritized capacity pool and applied temporary rate shaping to reduce queuing. You may still observe higher latency for long-sequence requests. We expect measurable improvement within 45 minutes. For high-priority tenants, please contact your CSM for a dedicated brief. — Redwood Operations"

3) Resolution message:
Subject: Incident resolved — monitoring
Body: "The issue impacting inference latency in us-west-2 has been resolved. We are monitoring telemetry and will follow up with a detailed post-incident report within 48 hours. If you observed errors or data loss, please reply with details and we will investigate. — Redwood Operations"

Escalation thresholds (summary table as text):
- P0: Availability <99.9% across region or >5% of requests returning 5xx — exec alert and immediate customer comms.
- P1: Sustained P99 latency above target for 15+ minutes for >10% traffic — status page + hourly updates.
- P2: Localized degradation affecting <10% of tenants or transient spikes — internal channels only unless persistent.

Evidence collection & minimum artifacts (must be attached to the incident ticket):
- Raw metric queries (timestamped) showing SLO deviation.
- Traffic dump sample (redacted) for impacted requests (request id, timestamp, model, prompt length).
- Snapshot of kv-cache hit rates and eviction counts.
- Runtime traces: top-5 blocking goroutines / kernels.
- Any config changes (git commit id, deploy id) in the last 24h.

Automated runbook invocation examples (CLI snippets):
- Trigger reserved pool scale: rwoodctl capacity scale --pool reserved-usw-2 --replicas 3 --reason "incident INC-XXXX"
- Route traffic away from region: rwoodctl routing set-priority --region us-west-2 --priority 10 --reason "latency surge"

Game day & learning cadence (quarterly):
Objectives:
- Validate handover checklist under fatigue (long-running incidents).
- Practice multi-shift handover with synthetic noise and partial evidence.
- Exercise customer communications cadence and status page publication.

Example schedule (3-hour exercise):
- 00:00–00:20: Alert injection + initial triage
- 00:20–01:00: Bridge established, first mitigations applied, status page posted
- 01:00–02:00: Introduce asymptomatic regression (model-quality), require specialist escalation
- 02:00–02:30: Shift handover simulation (documented handoff)
- 02:30–03:00: Wrap-up and fast postmortem (lessons + action items)

Postmortem minimum template (to be completed within 48 hours):
- Title, incident ID, severity, start/end times
- Executive summary (3–4 sentences)
- Timeline (minute-resolution for first 2 hours, then 5–15 minute buckets)
- Root cause hypotheses and evidence supporting/rejecting each
- Corrective actions (owner + ETA)
- Preventative actions and follow-up (owner + ETA)
- Customer impact summary and communications timeline
- Attachments and links to artifacts

Runbook governance notes:
- Only documented, reviewed runbook actions may be executed by first responders without additional approval.
- Ad-hoc mitigations must be recorded and reviewed in the postmortem.

Operational tips and common pitfalls:
- Avoid over-communication: prefer precise, scheduled status updates rather than continuous minor posts that confuse customers.
- When routing traffic, include canary windows and verification checks to prevent oscillation.
- Preserve ticket evidence: screenshots and short-lived logs should be archived to the incident ticket quickly (within 2 hours) to prevent loss.

Appendix: Quick slack templates (incident channel)
- T+10m: ":rotating_light: INC-<id> — Investigating elevated latency in us-west-2. Initial triage: autoscaling triggered; investigating cache eviction. Bridge: <link>."
- T+60m: ":hourglass_flowing_sand: INC-<id> — Mitigation applied (traffic reroute). Still degraded for 10% of traffic. Next update in 30m."

Document ownership and review cadence:
- Owner: Service Reliability (eng-sre)
- Review cadence: quarterly or after any P0/P1 postmortem

Related pages and references:
- Incident evidence collection standard
- Runbook library index
- Status page publishing guide

If you have questions or want this playbook adapted for a specific product (Dedicated / Private deployments), contact the owner or the oncall rota manager.
